name: Dark Energy Camera (DECam)
description: The Dark Energy Survey Collaboration built a wide-field mosaic camera with thick fully depleted CCDs for the Blanco 4 m telescope in Chile. Its 570-megapixel focal plane includes imaging, guiding and focus devices.

places.note: The collaboration first assembled and tested the camera at Fermilab.
Víctor M. Blanco 4 m telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory.

date.basis: Official first-light night in UT, as dated by the instrument paper.

events.statement: DECam produced official first-light images on the Blanco telescope at Cerro Tololo.

evidence.supports: Dates the official first-light night and records the imaging results.
The collaboration distinguishes first-light images from commissioning and Science Verification.

date.basis: Start of campaign imaging reported by the project.

events.statement: The Dark Energy Survey began its southern-sky mapping campaign with DECam.

evidence.supports: Names the camera, its location and the start of survey data taking.

date.basis: The project confirms January 2019 as the final observing month. Sources use different day labels for the final night.

events.statement: The Dark Energy Survey finished collecting campaign data with DECam.

evidence.supports: The project retrospective confirms the final observations.

date.basis: UTC date of observations stated in the observer circular.

events.statement: A separate observing programme used DECam on the Blanco telescope to image the field of GRB 261108D.

evidence.supports: Direct observing report identifying telescope, instrument, date and programme.

earliest_record.rationale: This record is anchored to the official first-light demonstration of the integrated on-telescope camera. Preassembly and tests occurred at Fermilab.

links.statement: DECam scaled the LBNL fully depleted CCD technology into a large-format mosaic. LBNL supplied the later devices that Fermilab packaged.
links.scope: The LBNL detector design family and the 250 μm generation built for DECam.

evidence.supports: The delivered camera uses the LBNL-developed thick, fully depleted CCD design and the paper documents supply to Fermilab.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs beginning ‘Early in the planning’, ‘Manufacture’, and ‘The DECam chips’
evidence.supports: The supplier documents continuity of the detector technology from Berkeley's mid-1990s work to the manufacture of the 250 μm DECam devices.

evidence.locator: Slide 12, Key features of early project development
evidence.supports: The receiving project manager identifies the prior CCD programme that DES drew on and the manufacturing scale-up needed for the camera.

why: The survey required high detector sensitivity toward the red end of the optical spectrum. Berkeley's back-illuminated, fully depleted silicon CCDs met the survey's z-band sensitivity requirement.
caveats: The camera served multiple observing programmes. The original DES campaign ended in January 2019.
